description: Burning Issues, Cool Solutions: San Francisco’s Heat and Air Quality Resilience Plan is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Climate Health Program; San Francisco Department of Public Health; City and County of San Francisco, CA. The 2017 Labor Day Heat Wave helped San Francisco's Health Department recognize that they lacked a proactive plan to deal with extreme heat and wildfire smoke. Ten community-based organizations worked with public, private, and academic partners to co-develop a plan to increase the City's resilience to future events. Coverage: the United States (2024). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
